findings.title: Declare the meter's new exposure-buffer compute read
findings.trigger: Automatic exposure with NoScreenTrace, including native rendering.
findings.expected: The meter reads the producing exposure through an explicit dependency that makes the exposure-buffer write visible to compute shaders.
findings.statically_predicted_problem: The shader now reads exposureStops, but ExposurePass.Record declares only its image accesses and histogram access. Graphics ShaderRead covers vertex and fragment stages only. With screen tracing disabled, the earlier compute-read declaration is absent. FSR declares its compute read after the meter, so it cannot supply the missing dependency before this dispatch. The resource-state chain therefore omits this new read, leaving portable visibility of the exposure value unestablished.
evidence: exposure_meter.comp:15 introduces ExposureBlock; line 31 reads exposureStops.
Passes/ExposurePass.cs:63-66 prepares HDR, distance and histogram, then flushes without declaring Exposure.Buffer.
Vulkan/ResourceState.cs:170-178 distinguishes graphics ShaderRead from ComputeRead.
Passes/ScreenTracePass.cs:163 supplies ComputeRead only when that pass exists.
Passes/UpscalePass.cs:119 supplies ComputeRead after the meter.
findings.remedy: Declare Exposure.Buffer as ComputeRead before the meter's barrier flush. Add a focused validating regression with automatic exposure, screen tracing disabled and consecutive frames.

reproduction.recipe: Render consecutive changing-luminance frames with AutoExposure, NoScreenTrace, NoUpscaling and synchronization validation enabled. Check validation and compare histogram-derived exposure with the CPU reference.
reproduction.limitation: This is a static synchronization finding. No stale histogram or validation failure was reproduced during this read-only review.

findings.title: Make the binding architecture describe the implemented source boundary
findings.problem: The newly written composite example divides both indirect terms by exposure. The implementation keeps fresh ambient and volume terms in scene units and divides only stored glossy history. The example describes the behavior that the ambient correction removed. The new scene-radiance section also retains the superseded 8192/16384 response.
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:1606-1614 presents unconditional indirectDiffuse and indirectSpecular exposure removal.
Shaders/composite_pass.glsl:90-101 obtains fresh scene-unit terms and removes exposure only from the stored glossy-history contribution.
ARCHITECTURE.md:2606 states identity through 8,192 and an asymptote of 16,384.
Shaders/bloom_prefilter.frag:26-29 implements identity through 128 and an asymptote of 256.

evidence.source: User: one model for old and new; one authoritative representation
evidence.assessment: The original scene HDR remains the source for metering and bloom. Emission/direct attachments are shading intermediates. FSR color and bloom levels are derived consumer representations with explicit conversion points.

evidence.source: Ousterhout: information hiding and deep modules
evidence.assessment: BloomPass derives mapping values from FrameContext. Callers do not supply a second source image or maintain a separate exposure copy. UpscalePass owns its input conversion.

evidence.source: User: keep state transitions under their owner
evidence.assessment: The exposure buffer remains under ExposureResources and ExposurePass. FrameGraph places adaptation after display consumers. C1 is an omitted resource-use declaration within that arrangement; it needs a local correction.

The shared finite-product helper serves display exposure, estimator conversion, falloff and bloom strength. closedFormScene supplies one ambient implementation, with the bounded wrapper serving history consumers.
CompositePass owns and initializes the disabled-history image. Scene attachments no longer double as history-format placeholders. The tone-map encoding flag is derived from the actual upscale target.

validation_gaps: F1 records documentation obscurity separately. It must be fixed even though the implemented ownership model is coherent.
Saved pooled metrics are incomplete population measurements. They do not prove the design of each changed type.
Consumer hardening assigned to #4 is outside the focused BloomPass coverage and selected source-mutant evidence.
